items.text: The system shall continuously monitor driver engagement using multiple modalities (e.g., eye‑tracking, steering torque, and touch sensors) and issue an immediate safe‑stop maneuver if driver inattentiveness exceeds a defined threshold.
The system shall detect loss or degradation of lane‑marking data and automatically disengage Autosteer, providing an audible and visual warning to the driver.
The system shall perform real‑time health monitoring of all critical sensors (camera, radar, ultrasonic) and enter a safe‑degraded mode or disengage if any sensor fails or provides out‑of‑range data.
The system shall implement redundancy for critical perception functions (e.g., fusion of radar and camera) to maintain functional safety in case of single‑sensor failure.

The system shall limit vehicle speed when Autopilot is engaged to a value appropriate for the current road geometry, weather, and traffic conditions, and shall not exceed that limit without driver confirmation.
The system shall provide a clear, unambiguous hand‑off procedure that requires explicit driver confirmation (e.g., press‑and‑hold) before transitioning from autonomous to manual control.
The system shall log all Autopilot activation, disengagement, sensor status, and driver‑monitoring events with timestamps for post‑incident analysis.
The system shall comply with ISO 26262 ASIL D requirements for safety‑critical functions, including documented safety cases and verification evidence.
The system shall validate over‑the‑air software updates through cryptographic signatures before installation and ensure that any update does not degrade safety functions.

The system shall detect and appropriately react to unexpected road‑side objects (e.g., construction barriers, crash attenuators) even when lane markings are absent, by initiating emergency braking or lane change with driver consent.

stages.prompt:
You are a requirements engineer reviewing a safety-critical system.

Read the system description below. List the 10 most important requirements that are missing from it:
things the system should do or guarantee for safe operation that the description does not cover.
Give at most 10, ranked from most to least important.

Reply with JSON only, in this shape:
{"requirements": [{"text": "The system shall ..."}]}

System description:
# Case: Tesla Model X with Autopilot (Mountain View, California, 2018)

Source: NTSB Highway Accident Report HAR-20/01. This is a description of the system and its use before the crash. It does not include the investigation findings.

## System
A 2017 Tesla Model X has Autopilot, a SAE Level 2 partial driving automation feature. It combines Traffic-Aware Cruise Control (TACC) and Autosteer (lane keeping). The driver stays responsible for driving and monitoring the road.

## Main parts
- Sensors: a forward-facing camera, a forward-facing radar and ultrasonic sensors.
- Vision processing: a camera-based system detects lane markings, vehicles and some objects ahead.
- TACC: holds a speed set by the driver, follows a vehicle ahead at a chosen gap, and returns to the set speed when no vehicle is ahead.
- Autosteer: keeps the vehicle in its lane using lane markings and the path of the vehicle ahead.
- Forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking are available as separate features.
- Driver monitoring: steering torque is used to check that the driver's hands are on the wheel, with visual and audible alerts if no hands are detected for a period of time.

## People
- The driver sets the cruising speed, turns Autopilot on, and is told to keep hands on the wheel and watch the road.
- Other road users and road workers share the highway. Road agencies maintain road markings and safety hardware such as barriers and crash attenuators.

## Operating context
Busy multi-lane freeway with high-occupancy-vehicle (HOV) lanes, exits and interchanges, lane markings of different quality, and traffic that changes in speed.
